pairs.question: Nonne satis tibi est hinc quod ait Tullius: amicitia est rerum humanarum et divinarum cum benevolentia et caritate consensio?
pairs.answer: Si tibi sufficit ista diffinitio, mihi iudico satisfactum esse.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels 'Aelredus.' (before the question) and 'Ivo.' (before the answer), the title lines, the CAPUT headers, and the trailing Latin-Library footer. Aelred asks (real interrogative, 'Nonne...?') whether Tullius's quoted definition suffices; Ivo answers affirmatively that he is satisfied. Answer is its single full sentence; nothing cut.

pairs.question: Quid est igitur quod inter amicissimos graves ortas inimicitias legimus?
pairs.answer: Haec volo interim credas numquam fuisse amicum, qui laedere potuit eum quem in amicitia semel recepit; sed nec eum verae amicitiae gustasse delicias qui vel laesus desiit diligere quem semel amavit.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels 'Ivo.'/'Aelredus.'. Ivo asks (interrogative 'Quid est... quod') how enmities can arise among the closest of friends. Aelred's reply opens with a non-answering deflection, 'De his suo loco uberius, si Deus voluerit, disputabimus.' ('we will discuss this at length elsewhere'); the answer start is advanced past it to the operative answering sentence, which explains that such people were never true friends. Window ends at the first full stop, before 'Omni enim tempore diligit qui amicus est.'

pairs.question: Nonne sapientia multi abutuntur, qui ex ea hominibus placere cupiunt, vel in seipsis pro collata sibi sapientia superbiunt; vel certe hi qui eam venalem habent, et quaestum estimant pietatem?
pairs.answer: Hinc tibi satisfaciet noster Augustinus, cuius verba sunt haec: qui sibi placet, stulto homini placet; quia profecto stultus est, qui sibi placet.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels 'Ivo.'/'Aelredus.' and dropped the asking-framing interjection 'quaeso te' ('I ask you') from inside the question, leaving the speaker's own words in source order. Real interrogative ('Nonne... abutuntur?') asking whether wisdom is abused; Aelred answers by citing Augustine that whoever abuses wisdom does not in fact have it. Answer ends at the first full stop, before 'Qui vero stultus est, sapiens non est...'.

pairs.question: Quid si pessimi quique vel ethnici in consensu facinorum et flagitiorum sic se diligant, ut velint pro invicem mori, eos ne ad summam amicitiae conscendisse fatebimur?
pairs.answer: Absit; cum inter pessimos amicitia esse non possit.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels 'Galterus.'/'Aelredus.'. Galter asks (interrogative '...eos ne... fatebimur?') whether the wicked who would die for one another have reached the summit of friendship; Aelred answers no, since friendship cannot exist among the wicked. Whole reply kept; nothing cut.

pairs.question: Quid igitur nobis cum amicitia, qui boni non sumus?
pairs.answer: Ego bonum non ita ad vivum reseco, ut quidam qui neminem volunt esse bonum, nisi eum cui ad perfectionem nihil desit.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels 'Galterus.'/'Aelredus.'. Galter asks (interrogative 'Quid... nobis cum amicitia') what they have to do with friendship since they are not good; Aelred answers by redefining 'good' more loosely, so that they qualify. Window ends at the first full stop, before 'Nos hominem bonum dicimus, qui...'.

pairs.question: Si prospera nostra nulla umquam adversitas interpolet, quomodo amici probabitur fides?
pairs.answer: Multa sunt alia quibus probatur fides amici, quamuis in sinistris maxime.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels 'Gratianus.'/'Aelredus.'. Gratian asks (interrogative 'quomodo... probabitur fides') how a friend's faith is tested if no adversity ever interrupts prosperity; Aelred answers that there are many other ways it is proved, though most of all in misfortune. Answer is its single full sentence; the following sentence ('Nam ut superius diximus...') is left out.
